name: Worldwide stations
source: NOAA Worldwide Marine Radiofacsimile Broadcast Schedules (7 March 2025); NWS USCG broadcast pages; 47 CFR 80.1077 (GMDSS, search and rescue); Australian Bureau of Meteorology; Priyom (French Navy, HFGCS, RAF voice, Russian military, numbers stations, November 2026); Numbers & Oddities 343-348, April to September 2026 (numbers stations); HF Underground (pirates, 2022 and 2024); ITU Radio Regulations Appendix 17 (HF marine channels); 47 CFR 95 (CB); G4NSJ (Volmet, LDOC); Milcom Monitoring Post (NAT, 2015); hfunderground wiki (DWD RTTY, ZLM); udxf.nl (HFDL); Wikipedia (time signals, long wave at September 2026, broadcast bands); ARISS station status, 27 October 2026 (ISS); AMSAT FM and linear satellite frequency summaries, 31 October 2026 (satellites); oz7igy.dk and GB3NGI's keeper (beacons); Motorola Solutions and the PMR446 and LPD433 channel plans (licence-free bands); IARU Region 1 (amateur emergency centres); ARRL (Hurricane Watch Net, FEMA 60 m); RadioReference wiki, May 2025 (US Coast Guard).
note: For listening only: nothing here is yours to transmit on, and most is someone's safety or working traffic. Some countries, the UK among them, make it an offence to listen to messages not meant for you or to pass them on. These lists come from public and hobby sources of varying age, so a flag doesn't promise a signal.
